subject: OKR prioritization, cross-functional playbook & final signoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>; laura.bennett@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai; evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@redwood.ai; diane.cho@venturecap.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OKR prioritization proposal + cross-functional playbook (Q4)

Team —

Attached is the first pass of the Q4 OKR playbook and my proposed prioritization for leadership sign-off. I tried to keep this focused and executable; highlights below: 

1) Top-level OKRs (proposed)
  - O1: Reduce 99th percentile inference latency by 20% across hosted models
    * Key result: Move 65% of steady-state traffic to optimized quantized variants
  - O2: Drive unit-cost down 18% on the top 3 revenue-generating routes
    * Key result: Implement KV caching and adaptive batching on 2 high-volume services
  - O3: Launch Dedicated GA and secure first 3 paid contracts
    * Key result: Close two mid-market deals and one enterprise pilot

2) Trade-offs / asks
  - We need to defer the exploratory RAG-ops initiative unless we expand Dedicated capacity (resource constraint).
  - Product will own rollout gating; Eng (Marcus) to confirm capacity impact.

3) Proposed timeline:
  - Nov 1: Final sign-off for OKR wording + metrics
  - Nov 10: Playbook published to Console + team distribution
  - Nov 15: QBR prep packet complete

Attachments: Q4_OKR_playbook_v1.pdf (draft playbook)

Ask: Please review and reply with either SIGNOFF, MINOR_EDITS, or MAJOR_CONCERNS by COB Oct 31. If you have capacity objections, flag them with concrete numbers.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Product & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai; evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR prioritization proposal + cross-functional playbook (Q4)

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear readout. Quick notes inline and at a high level: 

> - O1: Reduce 99th percentile inference latency by 20% across hosted models
>   * Move 65% of steady-state traffic to optimized quantized variants

I support this objective but suggest we split the key result: one KR for quantization adoption (60% traffic target) and a separate KR for latency SLO (99p < target ms). That makes it clearer for SRE/console dashboards.

> - O2: Drive unit-cost down 18% on the top 3 revenue-generating routes

We should tie this to revenue buckets (search vs. assistant vs. ingestion) — I'll add specific route names in the next pass. Also: we need an acceptance criteria for 'no more than 5% quality regression'.

Minor ask: please add a one-line owner for each KR (Eng/Product/Finance) — helps for QBR callouts.

Tentative: MINOR_EDITS. Will drop exact route names by Oct 30.

Laura Bennett
SVP, Revenue
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; laura.bennett@laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR prioritization proposal + cross-functional playbook (Q4)

Karthik / Laura —

Thanks for the callouts. From an engineering capacity perspective: the quantization push + adaptive batching work will require sustained allocation on two infra teams (runtime and scheduler) for ~8 weeks each. I attached a quick estimate with headcount-days and probable infra spend. If we keep the RAG-ops effort, that's an additional ~28 headcount-days in Nov which will push back the latency work.

Proposal: move RAG-ops to backlog for Q4 and prioritize O1/O2. If leadership wants to stretch for RAG-ops, we need to trade off the batch timeline (delay by 3 weeks) or add contractor support.

Attachment: capacity_impact_estimate.xlsx

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; laura.bennett@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR prioritization proposal + cross-functional playbook (Q4)

Quick note: I agree with prioritizing latency and cost reductions over RAG-ops for Q4 given sales commitments. I have a couple of tweaks for the playbook around rollout gating and SLO rollback behavior that I'd rather discuss live (two items that affect alerting and runbooks).

Can we do a 20-minute sync today at 11:00 PT to finalize owners? I've sent a calendar invite (placeholder).

Evelyn
Head of Reliability & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai; marcus.lin@redwood.ai; evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: Diane Cho <diane.cho@venturecap.com>; Matt Klein <matt.klein@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: OKR playbook v2 attached — ready for final signoff

Team —

Thanks for the rapid feedback and for the sync today. I've incorporated:
  - Split O1 KRs into quantization adoption + explicit 99p latency target
  - Added owners for each KR (Product / Eng / Finance / Ops)
  - Removed RAG-ops from Q4 and marked as backlog with a trigger for Q1 revisit
  - Added 'quality regression' acceptance criteria (<=5%) under O2
  - Added rollout rollback runbook notes per Evelyn's comments

Attachments: Q4_OKR_playbook_v2.pdf; capacity_impact_estimate.xlsx

Ask: Leadership, please reply with SIGNOFF in-thread by EOD Nov 4 if you approve. After signoff I'll publish the playbook to the leadership wiki and kick off the Canaries runbook work with Ops.

External note: Diane and Matt — FYI on prioritization and delivery timeline (we'll send a customer-facing note once we lock the playbook).

Karthik
VP, Product & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
